title: Dr. Rajesh Talwar & Smt. Nupur Talwar v. State of UP & CBI (Aarushi-Hemraj Case)
crime_type: Double Homicide / Circumstantial Evidence / Forensic Contamination
court_or_authority: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad / Special CBI Court, Ghaziabad
legal_citation: Criminal Appeal No. 6147/2013; 2017 SCC OnLine All 2237; 2018 CriLJ 681
source: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad Official Judgment & Indian Kanoon (doc/7921382)
ipc_sections: Section 302 r/w Section 34 IPC (Murder in furtherance of common intention)
Section 201 r/w Section 34 IPC (Causing disappearance of evidence)
Section 106 Indian Evidence Act 1872 (Burden of proving fact especially within knowledge)
location: Jalvayu Vihar, Sector 25, Noida, Uttar Pradesh, India

suspects.name: Krishna Thadarai
suspects.role: Initial Suspect (Discharged for lack of evidence)

evidence: Surgical-style throat incised wounds consistent with scalpel or sharp surgical blade
Blunt force cranial trauma inflicted by golf club (specifically club number 5 recovered from home)
Rooftop discovery of domestic help Hemraj Banjade's body 24 hours after initial scene processing
Forensic report typo in DNA typing of purple pillow cover recovered from room of Krishna
Scene of crime contamination by media and unmonitored visitors during the initial 48 hours
Internet router log analysis indicating active data connectivity in the master bedroom during nighttime hours
modus_operandi: Perpetrator accessed the locked flat during late hours, struck both victims (14-year-old Aarushi and 45-year-old domestic help Hemraj) on the head with a heavy blunt instrument, carried Hemraj to the roof, slit the throats of both victims with precision, arranged the crime scene, and locked the entrance doors.
personality_disorder: No confirmed psychopathology established. The Allahabad High Court noted that the trial court's theory of sudden grave provocation was conjectural and uncorroborated by objective psychiatric or physical evidence.
common_traits: Combination of blunt force trauma followed by precision sharp-force incision
Moving and concealing secondary victim's body on locked rooftop
Conflicting theories between two successive Central Bureau of Investigation teams
summary: India's most extensively scrutinized circumstantial homicide case. The Allahabad High Court reversed the trial court's conviction of the parents, ruling that the prosecution failed to establish an unbroken chain of circumstantial evidence beyond reasonable doubt, underscoring critical lessons in forensic preservation and confirmation bias.
